greeting.text: An old man sitting on the rail of a hulk with a stovepipe through its deck, his feet in a bucket of hot water. "Brindle's plate," Coll Darrow says, before you have finished. "Three suits and pieces, a pine crate, strapped. Hester sent you. Hester sends everybody." He moves his feet in the bucket. "I don't remember a thing about it."

choices.label: She says you'll remember the price to the penny.

greeting.text: Coll Darrow looks at the lid without lifting his feet out of the bucket. "Four crates at the Weir," he says. "Eleven gold, and I was glad of it. That's one of the four." He looks at the river. "I sold it to a carter who was going east. That's the whole of what I know, and it was the whole of what I wanted to."
Coll Darrow lifts one hand off the rail, which is as much greeting as his knees allow. "Blue rail," he says. "If you're looking for Lise. Tell her I asked after her. Don't tell her I said so."

"Up for the morning," Coll Darrow says, feet in the bucket. "Valley, by the boots." He nods at the end of the stones, where the wharf gives out into mud and river. "Go and stand there first, before you go in. I did it before every sale I ever walked into. Thirty years." He considers. "Never helped. Passed the time. Sometimes that's the same thing."

An old man on the rail of a hulk with a stovepipe, his feet in a bucket. "Retired," he says, to a question you have not asked. "Thirty years up every river there is. Now I go up and down these steps and that's my river."

the_price.text: "Eleven gold," Darrow says at once, and then looks annoyed with himself. "At the Weir. Weir Landing, two days above Greyhythe, where the carters meet the boats for the east road. Sold the crate to Abe Treen for eleven, which was a loss, and brought Hester back twenty, which was a bigger one, and nobody's ever thanked me for it." He sniffs. "Abe said he'd somebody up the east road who'd take it. I didn't ask who. You don't ask a carter his buyers, same as you don't ask a packman his."

interjections.text: Sera: "He lost money so the back room could be empty. That's the whole conspiracy."

asked_for.text: Darrow looks at you for a while over the bucket. "All right," he says. "Abe said, 'It's been asked for.' That's all. That's all he said." He shrugs, carefully, so as not to spill the water. "Carters say it. I say it. It means somebody wanted a thing and you're not going to tell anybody who. It doesn't mean anything else. Mostly."

choices.label: Abe Treen. Where is he now?

flat.text: Darrow looks at you flatly over the bucket, an old man who has been told he is holding something back by better liars than you. "Eleven gold," he says, as if that settles it. "At the Weir. To Abe Treen, who said he had a buyer up the east road. That's the whole of it."

choices.label: Abe Treen. Where is he now?

wat.text: "Dead." Darrow takes his feet out of the bucket and looks at them. "Two winters back. The fever at the Weir took eleven that year and Abe was one, and they buried him up there because it was cheaper than bringing him down." He points along the mud with his chin. "His wife's on the hulk with the blue rail. Lise. She kept his book. Carters keep books, if they can write. Abe could. Big careful hand."

interjections.text: Aldric takes off his hat, and puts it back on, as if he had not decided to.
